'''Seke''' (Serke, [[Tangbe]], Tetang, Chuksang) is a [[Tamangic languages|Tamangic language]], sometimes considered a separate language from [[Thakali language|Thakali]]. Seke is spoken in the villages of Tangbe, Tetang, Chuksang, Chaile, and Gyakar in [[Mustang District]], northern Nepal. Martine Mazaudon has documented the Tangbe dialect of Seke as spoken by an expatriate speaker in Paris.<ref>Mazaudon, Martine. 2023. ''The name of the Se(r)ke language and the reconstruction of a final -s in proto-TGTM (Tamangish)''. 26th Himalayan Languages Symposium, 4-6 September 2023. Paris: INALCO.</ref> Honda (2002) also documented two other dialects of Seke, Tetang and Chuksang.<ref>Honda, Isao. 2002. Seke phonology: a comparative study of three Seke dialects. ''[./Linguistics_of_the_Tibeto-Burman_Area Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area]'' 25(1): 191-210.</ref> 

== Geographical distribution ==
Seke is spoken by [[Gurung people|Gurung]] of Chuksang, Tsaile, Tangbe, Tetang, and Gyakar villages of [[Mustang District]], [[Dhawalagiri Zone]]. There are only 700 native speakers of this language, 100 of whom live in [[New York City]]. Reportedly, half of the New York City speakers live in the same apartment building.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Freytas-Tamura |first=Kimiko de |date=2020-01-07 |title=Just 700 Speak This Language (50 in the Same Brooklyn Building) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/07/nyregion/rare-languages-seke-vlashki-wakhi.html |access-date=2020-01-08 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Robbins |first=Christopher |date=2019-12-03 |title=Dazzling Map Shows NYC's Incredible Linguistic Diversity |url=https://gothamist.com/news/dazzling-map-shows-nycs-incredible-linguistic-diversity |access-date=2020-02-12 |website=Gothamist |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-09 |title=There's New Hope For Endangered Languages In NYC |url=https://newyork.cbslocal.com/2020/01/09/endangered-language-alliance-seke-nepal-new-york-city/ |access-date=2020-02-12 |language=en-US}}</ref>
